title: LLM prefetch + KV-cache PRD - scratchpad
content:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for an initial PRD outline exploring a proactive prefetch + KV-cache feature for the Redwood inference runtime/hosted API. Goal is to sketch user problems, user stories, acceptance criteria, rough metrics and open questions — not a final design.

Problem statement:
- For many products we see repeated, highly overlapping token prefixes across requests (e.g. system prompts + shared instructions + common user metadata).
- Cold KV-cache and model context compute is the dominant per-request cost for low-latency apps (chat assistants, tools, reranking).
- Current caching is reactive and per-request; misses opportunities to precompute/keep hot KV states for predictable workloads (scheduled agents, multi-turn flows, high-frequency users).

Proposed feature (high-level):
- "Prefetch + tenant-scoped KV cache": allow the control plane to mark certain prompt prefixes / model variants to precompute and persist KV-cache in memory (or fast storage) on serving nodes.
- Provide APIs for: (a) background prefetch jobs, (b) TTL and eviction policies, (c) hinting by route or customer to prioritize warm states, (d) metrics and cost accounting for kept states.
- Integrate with smart routing so requests can be routed to nodes already holding the warm KV state when low latency is required.

User personas & primary value:
- Product engineers building chat assistants: lower median latency, fewer token compute charges when warm states hit.
- Platform teams: better unit economics via fewer redundant compute cycles across similar requests.
- SRE/ops: predictable tail latencies for critical routes (can SLA-bound warm pool).

Examples / user stories:
1) As a PM building a customer support assistant, I want the assistant's system prompt + company policy prefix to be kept warm so that user messages return responses under 150ms p95.
   - Acceptance: p95 latency drops by >=30% for warm-hit requests, warm-hit rate >60% for traffic following common prefix patterns.
2) As an infra owner, I want to define a warm-pool for an enterprise customer with reserved capacity and TTL so I can guarantee latency SLAs during business hours.
   - Acceptance: warm pool can be scheduled, capacity observed, and daily cost attributed to customer billing.
3) As an SDK user, I can attach a "prefetch_hint" to a route so the system will schedule background prefetch for that model+prefix.
   - Acceptance: API documented; scheduling succeeds; prefetch failures surfaced in console.

Metrics to track (initial):
- Warm-hit rate by route/model/prefix
- Delta in per-request token compute (tokens avoided)
- Latency p50/p95 for warm vs cold
- Memory footprint of kept KV states (per-node, per-customer)
- Cost delta (ops cost vs expected savings)

Design considerations / constraints:
- Memory limits: KV states can be large for long contexts; need policy to bound size (truncate prefixes, quantize states?).
- Freshness: when model or prefix changes, invalidate or recompute automatically.
- Multi-tenant isolation: ensure one customer's warm states cannot evict another's in dedicated pools; enforce quotas.
- Model variants / quantization: compatibility rules for reusing states across model variants (e.g., same model version + quantization).
- Security: KV contains derived hidden state — treat as customer data, subject to KMS/audit when persisted.

Open questions / research spikes:
- How much memory does a typical prefix KV state consume for our top-5 models at sequence length 1024? (quick benchmark needed)
- Can we compress or shard KV states across nodes to reduce duplication?
- Prefetch scheduling: heuristics vs explicit customer hints — which gives best ROI?
- Cost model: define per-hour cost attribution for warm slots vs on-demand compute.

Rough rollout plan:
- Spike: implement profiler + benchmark to measure KV state sizes and compute cost of warming (2w)
- Alpha: expose internal-only prefetch job API; instrument warm-hit metrics; manual scheduling for a couple pilot customers (4w)
- Beta: SDK hinting API + console UI to manage warm pools, TTLs and billing visibility (6–8w)
- GA: formalize quotas, SLA docs, automated fallback routing + billing integration (8–12w)

Risks / tradeoffs:
- Warm pools consume memory and may increase infra cost; need strong telemetry to show net savings.
- Complexity in routing and consistency — may increase request routing fragility; need graceful fallback to cold-path.
- Potential security implications of persisting transient model state — legal review required for private deploys.

Next steps (my TODOs):
- Schedule micro-benchmark with serving-runtime team to measure KV sizes (owner: Samir)
- Draft small API sketch for prefetch_hint and warm-pool management (owner: me)
- Add a Confluence RFC stub and link here (owner: Zoe)
- Identify 2 pilot customers (via solutions-engineering) who care about low p95 latency

Notes to self / parking lot ideas:
- Consider a hybrid approach: LRU pool + predictive LSTM to prefetch next-k likely prefixes (overkill?)
- Explore cheaper persisted formats (e.g., quantized KV on NVMe + fast load path)
- Decide whether warm-states should be cross-node replicable or single-owner pinned

End of scratchpad. Mostly thinking aloud — move to a formal PRD once benchmarks are in and a clear cost story exists.
